figures.caption: Figure 1. Distance matrices for all ROIs and two representative networks computed using two different metrics. Each row and column corresponds to a scan session; each cell represents the distance between a pair of sessions. Darker colors represent larger distance.
Figure 2. Density plots for all ROIs and two representative networks comparing between-subject (red) and within-subject distances (blue) using Frobenius metric and AIRM.

Figure 3. Scatterplot for all ROIs comparing pairwise distances calculated using Frobenius metric and AIRM. Each point represents distance between a pair of sessions. Triangles indicate within-subject distances, colored by subject ID, while grey circles represent between-subject distances.
Figure 4. Scatterplot for two representative networks comparing pairwise distances calculated using Frobenius metric and AIRM.
Table 1. dbICC, bootstrap confidence intervals, MSDw, and MSDb computed under Frobenius metric and AIRM, across all ROIs and functional networks.
Figure 5. dbICC values under Frobenius metric and AIRM across different networks.

Figure 6. Scan length and dbICC values under Frobenius metric and AIRM, across all ROIs and functional networks. Each curve represents the dbICC values computed at different scan lengths for a specific network. The bottom x-axis is accumulated time point (TR = 2.2s) and the top xaxis is the scan length in minutes.
